Subject: Post-call recap + initial capacity ask (QuantumLytics POC)

Thanks again for the time this morning — really productive call. High-level recap and proposed next steps so we have alignment going into the POC kickoff:

Summary of needs:
- Workload: multimodal retrieval-augmented generation (RAG) with 1–2k token infra prompts, avg response length ~350 tokens.
- Target traffic during eval: 20–40 requests/sec peak; steady-state ~10 rps.
- Success criteria (customer-provided): p95 generation latency <= 120ms, 95% prompt-set pass rate for hallucination/accuracy tests, stable throughput for 1hr soak.

Initial capacity proposal (engineering preliminary):
- Reserved baseline: 2 x H100 (40GB) dedicated for the POC (predictable latency).
- Autoscaling/burst: add up to +4 H100 for spikes (total 6) with 10–15s warmup on cold scale; we recommend a short cache-warmup period.
- Fallback: smaller quantized variant (int8) available if warm start required for cold bursts.

Immediate asks / next steps:
1) QuantumLytics: confirm success criteria above and provide a short test prompt set (10–20 queries) and one representative dataset sample by EOD Thurs (11/23).
2) Procurement: indicate PO window — ideally we lock reserved capacity for the trial the week of 11/27.
3) Redwood internal: Rafael, can you confirm the burst profile (GPU bump timing and expected latency hit) and whether KV/prefix caching will meet their p95 SLA?

Attachment: QuantumLytics_POC_scope_v1.pdf (scope + eval checklist).

I'm happy to jump on a short 20-min kickoff once we have confirmation on success criteria and PO timing.

Best,
Ben

Quick technical plan and assumptions: 

Assumptions:
- Model variant: 7B RAG backbone (LLM + bi-encoder retrieval). Token lengths you stated are fine.
- Cold KV warmup: first 200 requests will see slower p95 while caches fill; recommend running a 20–30 min warmup run with representative prompts before formal soak.

Capacity recommendation (balanced for latency & cost):
- Baseline reserved: 2 x H100 (40GB) pinned to the POC. This gives predictable p95 for steady-state 10–12 rps.
- Autoscale burst: policy to add +1 H100 at 25 rps, +2 more at 35 rps, capping at 6 total (2 reserved + 4 burst). Burst nodes will be pre-warmed with model weights where possible (cold boot ~45–90s, warm pool ~10–20s).
- If QuantumLytics wants instant burst with sub-200ms p95, we should discuss a small warm pool (1–2 pre-warmed GPUs) as part of the reserved commitment.

Performance impact: expect median latency ~50–80ms on H100 for typical prompts; p95 depends heavily on cache hit rate and sequence length — anticipate p95 in the 90–140ms range during bursts unless warm pool enabled.

Integration notes on caching:
- Prefix/KV caching: no prompt reformat required; we support per-request cache keys and TTLs. Best practice: include a stable user/session id in the request metadata so cache is keyed consistently.
- Quantization path: we can provide an int8 variant for cost-pressure scenarios; accuracy degradation should be validated on the prompt set.

Attachment: poc-burst-plan.yaml (infrastructure snippet + autoscale policy).

I can run a quick smoke-run in staging once we have the prompt set. Rafael
